items.title: The Gentlemen ransomware hits Japanese manufacturer
items.summary: CYFIRMA's early-September intelligence report lists a Japan-based manufacturing company among new victims of The Gentlemen ransomware group.

items.title: Peru National Water Authority — Black Shrantac claims 2TB
items.summary: Black Shrantac claims a ransomware attack on Peru's National Water Authority, alleging theft of 2TB of hydrometeorological data, permits and technical documents.

items.title: Nike listed by WorldLeaks extortion group
items.summary: Nike appears among 2026 victims claimed by the WorldLeaks data-extortion group, per SharkStriker's running 2026 tracker.

items.title: Bitdefender September 2026 Threat Debrief
items.summary: Bitdefender's monthly debrief summarises leak-site victim volumes and the most active ransomware groups for September.

items.title: Black Kite: 7,551 ransomware victims in 12 months, up 24.9%
items.summary: Black Kite's 2026 report counts 7,551 publicly disclosed victims from April 2025 to March 2026, with government, retail and manufacturing most targeted.

ransomware.note: Thin named-victim coverage in today's search; the Peru and Nike claims come from a running 2026 tracker and exact September dating is unconfirmed.

items.title: Azure East US regional failure takes down ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok
items.summary: A regional Azure East US failure on Sep 3 caused roughly 90 minutes of outages across major AI services, with tens of thousands of user reports.

items.title: AWS confirms permanent data loss in Bahrain (me-south-1)
items.summary: AWS confirmed permanent data loss in its Bahrain region after damage spanning multiple Availability Zones — a reminder that multi-AZ is not multi-region.

items.title: Major hyperscalers report normal operation mid-September
items.summary: AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Akamai, DigitalOcean, Heroku and Vercel all reported normal status as of mid-September.

items.title: Forrester: two major multi-day hyperscaler outages expected in 2026
items.summary: Forrester predicts at least two multi-day hyperscaler outages this year as providers prioritise AI infrastructure over legacy systems.

outage.note: No new major hyperscaler outage found in the past week; the Sep 3 Azure event remains the month's headline.

items.title: CISA adds seven exploited flaws incl. SonicWall SMA1000, LiteLLM, JFrog Artifactory
items.summary: CISA's Sep 2 KEV update covers Sangoma Switchvox, Starlette, Kestra, LiteLLM, JFrog Artifactory and two SonicWall SMA1000 flaws under active exploitation.

items.title: Kestra CVE-2026-49869 exploited for reverse shells and crypto miners
items.summary: The Kestra OSS command-injection flaw was likely exploited since late June to gain shells, enumerate Docker environments and deploy miners.

items.title: Adobe zero-day CVE-2026-75650 exploited three days before hotfix
items.summary: Exploitation was first observed Sep 4 with Adobe's hotfix arriving Sep 7; it is among CISA's Sep 8 KEV additions, two of which were confirmed zero-days.

items.title: CISA adds one more exploited vulnerability (Sep 4)
items.summary: CISA added a further actively exploited vulnerability to the KEV catalog on Sep 4.

items.title: Eleven new exploited CVEs added to KEV this week
items.summary: Senserva counts 11 new KEV entries this week and 1,333 actively exploited non-Microsoft CVEs across 282 vendors, 244 linked to ransomware.

items.title: M 6.6 — 80 km ENE of Tadine, New Caledonia (Sep 25)
items.summary: USGS green alert, no tsunami flagged.

items.title: M 6.4 — 49 km NNE of Kainantu, Papua New Guinea (Sep 20)
items.summary: USGS green alert, no tsunami flagged.

items.title: Typhoon Dujuan strikes Japan
items.summary: Typhoon Dujuan left four dead and several missing in Japan in early September.

items.title: Deadly floods in Nepal, Tibet and the Philippines
items.summary: Deadly flooding hit Nepal and Tibet and separately the Philippines in early September, with heavy rain also flooding Mecca.

items.title: Deadly forest fires in Algeria
items.summary: Forest fires in Algeria caused fatalities in early September.

physical.note: Natural-event items are early-September; no newer major event surfaced in today's search.
